summary.text: The council's flood plain, flood prone area, overland flow path and coastal inundation layers do not show any of these for this parcel.

The council's property category dates the building to the 1990s, a period covered by Settled.govt.nz's guidance on leaky buildings, which discusses buildings mostly built between the late 1980s and the mid-2000s.

Based on what you told us, the building year you gave falls in that same decade and the cladding is monolithic, a plaster-style system that Settled.govt.nz also discusses in its leaky-building guidance; no free public source could confirm the cladding.
Your loan is not in the Reserve Bank's high-LVR (loan-to-value ratio) or high-DTI (debt-to-income ratio) categories, and because no existing debts were entered, the DTI shown assumes you have none.

LINZ records the title as Unit Title, which Settled.govt.nz says makes the owner a member of the body corporate, and the unittitles.govt.nz guide says the body corporate must insure the property to its full insurable value.

next_steps.text: Ask for the building's age and cladding details and consider a pre-purchase building inspection.
Ask whether the cladding is monolithic and consider a pre-purchase building inspection.
Request the body corporate rules, meeting minutes, maintenance plan and levy details.
Ask your lawyer for the body corporate's current levy amounts, budget and long-term maintenance plan.
Ask for the body corporate insurance policy and check whether you need separate cover for your unit and contents.
Ask your lawyer to obtain and review the LIM report and other property documents from the council.
Ask your lender what insurance evidence it requires and get insurance quotes early.
Check your private insurance policy for cover above the Natural Hazards Commission cap.
Ask your insurer and the Natural Hazards Commission which parts of the land are covered.
Ask your insurer about its own excess in addition to the Natural Hazards Commission excess.
Ask your insurer how the Natural Hazards Insurance levy appears in the quoted premium.
Ask a registered valuer about a current market valuation.
Ask insurers about past claims and flood exclusions before making an offer.
Check the council property file for geotechnical reports, or ask a geotechnical engineer for site-specific advice.
Ask your lender and lawyer what finance and insurance arrangements to confirm for an auction.
